turns.text: Thanks for coming in today. Could you tell me about your current role and what a typical day looks like for you?

Hello. I am logistics coordinator in a transport company in Brno. I work there since three years. My typical day, I check the orders in the morning and I make plan for drivers on dispečink. Then I communicate with carriers and customers about delivery.
Thank you, that gives me a clear picture of your morning. When a truck is late, how do you keep everything running?

When a truck is late, first I call the driver and ask where he is and how much delay it will be. Then I inform the customer immediately, because they must know about the problem. If it is big delay, I look for another carrier or I change the plan on dispečink for other drivers. I am responsible about the delivery, so I keep the customer updated until the truck arrive.
That's a clear, careful process, and I like how you keep the customer informed. How many companies do you work with each week?
Every week I work with about thirty companies. Around twenty are carriers and ten are regular customers. Some of them I contact every day, for example when we have urgent delivery.
Thirty companies every week is a busy job, and it's clear the customers matter to you. Could you tell me about the warehouse work you do each day?

Actually I don't work in the warehouse directly, I work in the office. But I cooperate with the warehouse every day. I send to them the information about loading, which truck comes and what time. When there is a problem with the cargo, I check it with warehouse manager and I tell the driver what to do.
So you link the office and the warehouse every day. Which companies send you goods each week?

Most goods come from our regular customers, for example from some factories and from one big e-shop in Czech Republic. I use TMS system every day and also Excel, so I see all orders and which truck is free.
So the system shows you the whole day in one place. What happens when two orders need the same truck?

When two orders need the same truck, first I check which order is more urgent and what is the deadline. If it is possible, I put both orders in one truck, but only when the cargo fit together. If not, I find another carrier for the second order and I inform the customer about the change.
That's a clear plan, and checking urgency first makes sense. Let me ask something different: which part of your job do you enjoy most?

I enjoy most when I solve a difficult situation. For example, when a truck is late and I find a new solution fast, so the customer is happy. I like also to work with people, because every day is different.
Solving a late truck quickly sounds very satisfying, and I can see why customers trust you. Tell me, what would you change about your daily routine?

I would change maybe the planning in the morning. Now I make many things manually in Excel and it takes me one hour. I would like to have more automatic plan in TMS, so I have more time for communication with carriers.
Automatic planning in TMS would give you more time for carriers, which sounds really useful. If I hired you tomorrow, what would be your first big task?

My first big task would be to learn your TMS settings and your carriers. Then I would make the morning planning more organized, maybe with templates in Excel, so we save time. I also want to meet the warehouse team and the drivers in first week.
Templates could save real time, so that is a sensible plan. Which firms send you goods, and how do you manage their orders each week?

judge.voice: Honestly, it felt like a real interviewer for a few minutes. The questions about late trucks and two orders on one truck were exactly Friday's material, and it never treated me as Czech. I liked that dispečink became "dispatch" instead of counting against me. But the partner asked about warehouse work after I said I sit in the office, and it asked about the same companies twice. The recap gave me no phrases to take into the room. The "Mission done" banner sat there while questions kept coming. I would use it again for the evening rehearsals, but I would want more logistics wording and the big mistakes caught. Worth the twenty minutes.
